titleTr: ABD hayatına alışmak: used to, be used to, get used to

grammar.topic: used to / be used to / get used to
explainTr: 'used to + fiil' geçmişte bıraktığın alışkanlığı anlatır: I used to walk to the market (eskiden yürürdüm). Olumsuz ve soruda 'use to' olur: I didn't use to drive. Did you use to live there?

'be used to + -ing' bir şeye alışık olmaktır: I'm used to driving here (artık alışığım). 'get used to + -ing' ise alışma sürecidir: I'm getting used to the cold (alışıyorum). Burada 'to' edattır, o yüzden fiil -ing alır.
En sık hata: 'I'm used to live' veya 'I used to living'. Pratik kural: 'used to' + yalın fiil = eskiden; 'used to' + -ing = alışık. Be/get fiilini görürsen -ing kullan.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'eskiden giderdim' ve 'gitmeye alışığım' farklı ekleri kullanır. İngilizcede ikisi de 'used to' görünür; ama biri yalın fiil ister (I used to go), diğeri -ing (I'm used to going). Be/get gelirse -ing gelir.

reading.title: Getting used to America
reading.text:
When Hafsa first arrived in the United States, almost everything felt unfamiliar. She was used to the narrow streets of Isparta, where neighbors greet each other every morning, and she was not used to driving on wide highways. The grocery store had forty kinds of cereal, and she often stood in the aisle for ten minutes, unable to choose.

The language was the biggest challenge. In Turkey she used to read English recipes and watch a few films, but understanding fast speech at a bank or pharmacy was something completely different. At first she felt awkward and hesitated before every phone call. "I used to be a confident person," she told Linda one afternoon. "Now I feel like a child."

Linda, who had moved from Texas twenty years earlier, smiled. "I remember that feeling," she said. "You will get used to it. It takes time, but one day you stop translating in your head." She suggested practicing with small tasks: ordering coffee, asking for directions, calling the library. Hafsa followed the advice, and slowly the tasks became routine.

Other changes were harder to see. Dinner at six o'clock instead of nine felt too early, and she missed the long family evenings. She also had to get used to cooking with different ingredients and to cold winters with snow up to her knees. On difficult days she cooked a big pot of lentil soup and invited Linda over, which made the apartment feel like home.

After two years, Hafsa noticed how much had changed. She no longer felt lonely at school meetings, and she was used to saying "excuse me" in the hallway with a smile. She even began to enjoy small American habits, such as bringing a coffee cup to every appointment. Still, she did not want to lose her own traditions. "I used to think I had to choose," she said to Emre. "Now I know I can keep both."

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Hafsa, how is your new schedule at the school?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Tiring! I'm not used to waking up at five thirty.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: You'll get used to it. When I started teaching, I used to hit the snooze button five times.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Yes, after a few months my body adjusted. What else is difficult?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: The students speak so fast. I'm still getting used to their slang.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Don't worry. I didn't use to understand teenagers either.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: And the cafeteria food is strange! In Turkey we used to eat soup for lunch.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Bring your own soup! Plenty of teachers do.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Good idea. Maybe I can heat it in the staff kitchen.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Of course. And in a month you'll wonder why you were worried.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I hope you're right. Thank you, Linda.

writing.promptTr: Türkiye'deki bir arkadaşına e-posta yaz. Eskiden neler yapardığını (used to), neye alışık olduğunu (be used to) ve neye alışmaya çalıştığını (get used to) anlat. 120-180 kelime yaz.
writing.promptEn: Write an email to a friend in Turkey. Use used to, be used to, and get used to.
frames: When I lived in Isparta, I used to ...
I am still getting used to ...
writing.model: Dear Selin, how are you? I am writing from Michigan, where winter has finally started. When I lived in Isparta, I used to visit my neighbors every afternoon, and we used to drink tea for hours. Here, people make appointments even for a coffee! At first I felt lonely, but now I am getting used to the schedule. I am also used to driving on the highway, which was terrifying last year. The language is still difficult sometimes. I am not used to understanding fast speech on the phone, but my neighbor Linda helps me practice every week. I did not use to be patient, yet this experience has taught me a lot. I miss your cooking and our long talks, but I am happy with my new life. I am even starting to enjoy the snow, which I could not tolerate at the beginning. Please write soon and tell me about your family. I hope we can see each other next summer. With love, Hafsa
checklistTr: Olumsuzda 'didn't use to' (used değil) yazdın mı?
E-postada selamlama ve kapanış var mı?
